correctness.rationale: Strict convexity gives u/x=-I1/(I2+r I0), with Ij the discounted moments on [0,h]. The sample multiplier is always less than 1, and exceeds -1 exactly when r/h² exceeds the normalized moment (I1 h/2−I2)/(I0 h²). Setting z=ρh gives ψ. At zero discount the multiplier lies in (−1/2,1). For positive z the derivative has sign K: its factorial-scaled coefficients vanish through degree 4, are positive in degrees 5–15, and are strictly negative for degrees ≥16 by the closed coefficient formula. Hence K/z^15 strictly decreases, starting positive and becoming negative by z=8. The limits −1/12 and 0 from above give a single positive maximum and exactly two neutral rates above the sampling threshold. For fixed positive ρ, F=2(1−e^(−z))z²ψ has F''=z(z−1)e^(−z), hence one positive zero; beyond it the numerator of (F/(1−e^(−z)))' is positive and increasing. This gives the unique crossing of φ=rρ². Independently derived moment and series checks and recomputed the constants (z†=7.66360518354401985…, H*=5.63013461640019324…) and both rate roots for h=6, r=1 via /workspace/branches/replay_1.py. Decimals are approximations and not interval-arithmetic certificates. The result is for repeated exact one-hold optimizers without terminal terms; it makes no general MPC stability claim.

value.rationale: A minimal exact sampled optimal-control model isolates a real qualitative effect of within-hold discounting: stronger discounting can both destroy and restore stability even with no cost-integration error. The peak gives an exact all-discount design guarantee and explains why fixing the discount instead yields a single sampling frontier. This is a substantive sharp stability classification within the stated one-step scope.
